name: Winterizing
summary: We flush and test the water system, empty the tanks and fill the lines with antifreeze, so your RV sits safely through the cold.
includes: Testing the water system and finding any problems
Filling the water system with antifreeze
bring: The keys to the unit and any compartment locks
No need to empty the tanks first: we do that as part of winterizing

faq.a: Before overnight temperatures start dropping below freezing. Around Concord that’s usually late October to November. Water left in the lines can freeze and split pipes and fittings.

Trailers and fifth wheels: $199. Motorhomes: $249 (one hour at the motorhome rate). Parts, like antifreeze, and HST are extra. If testing the water system turns up a problem, we tell you what it is and what the repair costs. No extra work without your OK.

faq.q: Do I need to empty the tanks before I bring it in?
faq.a: No. Emptying the tanks is part of winterizing.
No. Water damage, like soft floors or rotted walls, is a separate repair. We do those too: see leak detection and repair.

faq.q: Should I cover the roof and A/C for the winter?
faq.a: A cover keeps snow, ice and debris out of the A/C unit and off the roof. We offer A/C covers and roof covers; ask when you book.
